answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable bond tied to a unique, verifiable identity. Every agent locks an indivisible stake before it can earn, and random audits then sample workers to test whether each identity is genuinely distinct. An attacker minting clones to trade cedar, guard a jetty, or sell pigment must post a separate bond for every fake identity, so scaling to a thousand Sybils locks a thousand bonds upfront. If an audit exposes a clone, its whole bond is burned. Expected slashing loss then exceeds any stolen reward, so faking identities costs more than honest work.
